# What this notebook does

Mass cytometry is not widely available in clinical laboratories, so translation
would need a smaller panel that a common spectral flow cytometer can run. This
notebook asks how few markers can carry the predictive signal, and produces
**Figure 7**.

The test is deliberately conservative. Within each cross-validation fold, markers
are ranked by how much they separate the meta-clusters (between-meta-cluster
variance). At each panel size (from all 30 markers down to 6), cells are
reassigned to their nearest full-panel cluster center using only the retained
markers -- the cluster centers themselves are not recomputed. This measures how
well a smaller panel approximates the full-panel clustering; a real prospective
panel would require building the atlas from scratch on the reduced markers.

Figure 7 has three panels:

- **A** -- cluster preservation (the fraction of cells that keep their
  meta-cluster) versus panel size.
- **B** -- held-out prediction error (RMSE of the full model) versus panel size,
  against the titers-only baseline.
- **C** -- the top 15 markers, ranked by their consensus between-cluster
  variance, colored by marker type.

```{r paths}
# Edit these to your local copy of the intermediate data (not distributed; see
# README, Data Availability). The three marker-reduction tables below are
# precomputed per-fold results; nothing here re-runs cell reassignment.
FAST <- "/fast/datasets/flu_cellular_prediction"

MR_DIR   <- file.path(FAST, "post_hoc_5000", "marker_reduction")
PRES_CSV <- file.path(MR_DIR, "E2_preservation.csv")     # cluster preservation per fold/budget
PERF_CSV <- file.path(MR_DIR, "E2_marker_perf.csv")      # held-out MSE per fold/budget/antigen
RANK_CSV <- file.path(MR_DIR, "E2_marker_ranking.csv")   # marker ranking per fold
AGG_PATH <- file.path(FAST, "per_fold_atlas_5000", "aggregated", "E2_aggregated.RData")
```

```{r load}
if (all(file.exists(c(PRES_CSV, PERF_CSV, RANK_CSV)))) {
  pres_dt <- fread(PRES_CSV)
  perf_dt <- fread(PERF_CSV)
  rank_dt <- fread(RANK_CSV)
} else {
  # ---- Heavy compute: for each fold and each panel size, reassign cells to the
  #      nearest full-panel center using only the retained markers, rebuild the
  #      CLR features, and refit the full elastic net. This needs the raw CyTOF
  #      object and the atlas helpers (available from the corresponding author). ----
  stop("Marker-reduction tables not found; see Data Availability.")
}

# Titers-only baseline MSE (M1), for the reference line in Panel B.
load(AGG_PATH)             # provides overall_mse
m1_overall <- overall_mse[["M1_en"]]
BUDGETS <- c(30, 25, 20, 15, 12, 10, 8, 6)
```

# Figure 7

```{r fig7-panelA, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.5}
# --- Panel A: cluster preservation vs panel size (mean +/- SD across folds) ---
pres_agg <- pres_dt[, .(mean_match = mean(meta_match), sd_match = sd(meta_match)), by = budget]
p_a <- ggplot(pres_agg, aes(budget, 100 * mean_match)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2166ac", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "#2166ac", size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = 100 * (mean_match - sd_match), ymax = 100 * (mean_match + sd_match)),
                width = 0.5, color = "#2166ac") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 15, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  scale_x_reverse(breaks = BUDGETS) +
  labs(x = "Number of markers", y = "Cluster preservation (%)",
       title = "A. Cluster preservation vs panel size") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
p_a
```

```{r fig7-panelB, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.5}
# --- Panel B: held-out RMSE (full model, overall) vs panel size ---
# Per fold/budget, the overall MSE is the mean across the three antigens.
perf_dt[, overall_mse := mean(cluster_test_mse), by = .(fold, budget)]
perf_agg <- unique(perf_dt[, .(fold, budget, overall_mse)])[
  , .(mean_mse = mean(overall_mse)), by = budget]
perf_agg[, rmse := sqrt(mean_mse)]
rmse_baseline <- sqrt(m1_overall)

p_b <- ggplot(perf_agg, aes(budget, rmse)) +
  geom_line(color = "#d6604d", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "#d6604d", size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = rmse_baseline, linetype = "dotted", color = "gray50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 15, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  annotate("text", x = 28, y = rmse_baseline + 0.01, label = "M1 baseline RMSE",
           color = "gray40", size = 3, hjust = 0) +
  scale_x_reverse(breaks = BUDGETS) +
  labs(x = "Number of markers", y = "Test RMSE (full model, overall)",
       title = "B. Prediction performance vs panel size") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
p_b
```

```{r fig7-panelC, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
# --- Panel C: top 15 consensus markers, colored by marker type ---
consensus <- rank_dt[, .(mean_var = mean(between_meta_var)), by = marker][order(-mean_var)]
top15 <- consensus[1:15]

# Marker-type grouping for the 15-marker panel (lineage / homing / activation /
# differentiation), matching the manuscript's spectral-flow-compatible panel.
marker_type <- c(
  CD19 = "Lineage", CD20 = "Lineage", CD3 = "Lineage", CD4 = "Lineage",
  CD8 = "Lineage", CD21 = "Lineage",
  CXCR5 = "Homing", CCR6 = "Homing", CCR2 = "Homing",
  `HLA-DR` = "Activation", CD86 = "Activation", CD25 = "Activation", CD38 = "Activation",
  CD27 = "Differentiation", CD57 = "Differentiation")
top15[, type := factor(marker_type[marker],
                       levels = c("Lineage", "Homing", "Activation", "Differentiation"))]
type_colors <- c(Lineage = "#2166ac", Homing = "#1a9850",
                 Activation = "#d6604d", Differentiation = "#f4a460")

p_c <- ggplot(top15, aes(reorder(marker, mean_var), mean_var, fill = type)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = type_colors, name = "Marker type") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean between-meta-cluster variance",
       title = "C. Consensus top 15 markers (by between-cluster variance)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "right")
p_c
```

```{r fig7-numbers}
cat("Cluster preservation at 30 / 15 / 12 markers (per-fold mean):\n")
print(pres_agg[budget %in% c(30, 15, 12), .(budget, preservation_pct = round(100 * mean_match, 1))])
cat("\nTest RMSE at 30 vs 15 markers:\n")
print(perf_agg[budget %in% c(30, 15), .(budget, rmse = round(rmse, 3))])
```

Cluster preservation falls from 100% at the full panel to about 62% at 15
markers and 54% at 12, yet held-out RMSE stays below the titers-only baseline at
every panel size, because the elastic net does not depend on exact cluster
identity. The 15-marker panel is the best trade-off, reaching the minimum RMSE.
Its markers span lineage (CD19, CD20, CD3, CD4, CD8, CD21), homing (CXCR5,
CCR6, CCR2), activation (HLA-DR, CD86, CD25, CD38), and differentiation (CD27,
CD57) -- a combination practical for spectral flow cytometry.
